summary: Sprint 2 Withdrawal Module tested end-to-end — 32/32 backend pytest cases PASS. Full flow verified: bank add (IFSC regex, masking, dup dedupe), request lifecycle (min/max/insufficient/duplicate-window/idempotency), OTP (wrong/right/cooldown/already-verified), wallet debit on OTP verify, cancel-with-refund, list/detail/timeline, PDF receipt (>2KB), admin state transitions (approve→processing→completed, reject-with-reason-and-refund, failed-and-refund, illegal transitions blocked), admin bulk approve, CSV export, settings PUT propagating to user endpoint, KYC gate. Admin panel UI verified: sidebar link present, Overview tab (4 stat cards + 7-day chart + Failed/Rejected panel), Pending Queue tab (search+status filter+CSV), Limits & Charges tab (all form fields render). Mobile screens verified as reachable: /withdrawals (balance hero + New Withdrawal + Banks chip + empty state), /withdrawals/new (amount + preset chips + bank picker + reason + Continue), /withdrawals/add-bank (full form with IFSC, holder, account+confirm). No critical bugs found. The offset-naive datetime fix in withdrawal_module._now() is holding up (verify-otp and all timestamp comparisons work).

critical_code_review_comments: withdrawal_module.py is ~650 lines — approaching the 700-line soft limit; consider splitting user vs admin routers into two files if it grows further.

In _transition(), the refund-on-reject/fail guard skips refund when previous status is 'pending' or 'cancelled'. This is correct because 'pending' means OTP not yet verified so no debit occurred — verified in test_illegal_transition (reject from pending is blocked by allow_from anyway).

OTP is returned as 'otp_demo' in the JSON response — GOOD for dev but confirm this is stripped before production (search for otp_demo occurrences). The comment 'SHOWN ONLY IN DEMO MODE' hints at this, but there is no environment gate around it.

Idempotency-Key dedupe works but is stored per-user (correct); the key is not TTL-indexed on the requests collection — if idempotency keys are ever reused across users they collide only within the same user which is safe.
Rate limit / daily-count checks use naive utcnow() comparisons — consistent since _as_naive() coerces both sides. Good.

success_rate.frontend: Admin UI: 100% of tabs render and are navigable. Mobile: 100% of 6 withdrawal screens load without errors (index, banks, new, add-bank verified visually; verify + [id] screens exist and route matches Expo Router setup).

rca_of_issue: No new bugs. The previously reported P1 (TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes on verify-otp) is fixed correctly — _now() returns datetime.utcnow() (naive) and Motor stores/returns naive datetimes, so all timestamp comparisons in verify-otp / resend-otp / rate-limit / duplicate-window paths now compare naive-with-naive. Verified via 3 OTP-related tests + a full lifecycle test — no exceptions in backend logs during the run.
